deficits.evidence: no purpose-built sidewalk, only parked cars and building walls
deficits.suggestion: Construct a continuous sidewalk on the left side to separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic.

deficits.evidence: no purpose-built sidewalk, only parked cars and building walls
deficits.suggestion: Construct a continuous sidewalk on the right side to provide a safe walking space.

deficits.evidence: residential and commercial buildings on both sides create demand, but no designated crossing exists
deficits.suggestion: Install a marked pedestrian crossing to facilitate safe movement between the two sides of the street.

deficits.evidence: no street lamps visible along the urban road segment
deficits.suggestion: Install street lighting along the road to improve visibility and safety at night.

ratings.reason: The left side is fully occupied by parked cars and building walls, leaving no physical space to construct a sidewalk.
The right side is also lined with parked vehicles and buildings, making the construction of a new sidewalk impossible without removing existing infrastructure.
No marked crossing is visible, but the suggestion to 'build a footway' is a mismatch for a crossing, and the tight space makes feasibility unclear.
No street lamps are visible in the frames, and installing them is a standard and feasible measure for this type of urban street.
